record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: If a finitely generated graded R-module M has finite complexity c = cx_R(M), does there exist a real constant a such that b_i^R(M)/i^{c-1} converges to a as i tends to infinity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a commutative Noetherian local ring (or a standard graded k-algebra over a field k), and let M be a finitely generated (graded) R-module. Denote by b_i^R(M) = dim_k Tor_i^R(M,k) the i-th Betti number of M. The complexity of M is defined by

  cx_R(M) = inf { d ∈ Z_{≥0} : there exists C > 0 with b_i^R(M) ≤ C · i^{d-1} for all i ≫ 0 },

and is assumed to be finite. Set c = cx_R(M), and assume c ≥ 1.

Question: Does there necessarily exist a real number a (depending on M) such that

  lim_{i → ∞}  b_i^R(M) / i^{c-1}  =  a ?

That is, when the Betti sequence of M has polynomial growth of degree exactly c − 1, must the normalized sequence b_i^R(M)/i^{c-1} converge to a (finite, nonnegative) limit?
artifact.category_tag: Betti numbers and complexity of modules
artifact.status_search_result: Over a complete intersection local ring, it is classical that the even- and odd-indexed Betti subsequences of a finitely generated module are eventually polynomial in i with leading terms of degree c−1; Avramov–Packauskas–Walker (2018+) showed that these two polynomials agree in their top several terms, in particular sharing the same leading coefficient, which yields existence of the limit lim b_i / i^{c-1} in the complete-intersection case. Recent work (e.g., "Polynomial growth of Betti sequences over local rings", arXiv:2208.04770, 2022–2024, and "Derived complete intersections and polynomial growth of Betti numbers over dg-algebras", arXiv:2605.11105) extends polynomial-growth results to broader settings, but in full generality (arbitrary local/graded R with M of finite complexity) the convergence of b_i(M)/i^{c-1} appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial growth of Betti sequences over local rings
status_evidence.snippet: Over a complete intersection, even- and odd-indexed Betti numbers are eventually polynomial in i with equal leading terms; further terms beyond a certain degree are shown to agree.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence of b_i/i^{c-1} is known in the complete intersection case via equality of leading terms of the even/odd Betti polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Derived complete intersections and polynomial growth of Betti numbers over dg-algebras
status_evidence.snippet: A derived version of Gulliksen's theorem characterizes dg-algebras over which finitely generated modules have polynomial Betti growth.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial Betti growth is tied to (derived) complete intersection structure; general convergence of normalized Betti sequences is studied but not settled in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Complete intersection dimension (Avramov–Gasharov–Peeva)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces complexity and complete intersection dimension and establishes polynomial bounds on Betti numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework for complexity used in the problem; does not establish convergence of b_i/i^{c-1} in general.
